from PIL import Image

def count_magnets_in_image(image_path):
    # Open the image using the Pillow library
    img = Image.open(image_path)

    # Initialize a dictionary to keep track of the magnets in the image
    magnet_db = {}

    # Detect the magnets in the image
    for i in range(img.width):
        for j in range(img.height):
            # Get the magnet label by examining the red colors
            # Get the magnet label by examining the red colors
            if img.getpixel((i, j)).red > 150:
                label = f"magnet:{i},{j}"
                # Check if the magnet label already exists in the dictionary
                if label in magnet_db.keys():
                    magnetic_position = magnet_db[label]
                    mag_x, mag_y = magnetic_position
                    new_x, new_y = (i, j)
                    # Update the coordinates of the magnet
                    magnet_db[label] = (new_x, new_y)
                    # Check if the new coordinates are within the magnet boundaries and if the new magnet does not overlap with a magnet that is already present
                    if new_x > mag_x and new_y > mag_y and new_x < ((i + 1) + (mag_x - mag_y)) and new_y < ((j + 1) + (mag_y - mag_x)):
                        # Remove the old magnet from the dictionary
                        del magnet_db[label]
                        break
    return magnet_db

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Image data from the problem statements
    image_paths = [
        "/home/stud/wxie/BLINK_Dataset/Counting/val/images/val_Counting_45_image_1.jpg"
    ]

    final_result = {"magnets_detected": 0}

    for image_path in image_paths:
        magnet_db = count_magnets_in_image(image_path)
        final_result["magnets_detected"] += len(magnet_db.keys())

    print(final_result["magnets_detected"])

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from Motor.Detection import obj_detector

# Function to save object images with bounding boxes and labels
def save_obj_with_bbox_labels(img_path, obj_list, bboxes, save_path):
    for obj, box in zip(obj_list, bboxes):
        bbox = {f"{obj}_{bbox_key}": bbox_key for bbox_key in "x1 y1 w h".split()}
        name = type(obj).__name__
        label = f"{name};{obj};{f'xmin {bbox['x1']}; xmax {bbox['x2']}; ymin {bbox['y1']}; ymax {bbox['y2']}}"
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(5, 5))
        ax.imshow(img_path)
        ax.scatter(*bbox.values(), color='red', marker='^', linewidth=1)
        plt.title(label)
        plt.axis('off')
        plt.savefig(f"{save_path}_{bbox['xyz']}.png")
        plt.close(fig)

# Function to detect objects in the bus image
def detect_objects(image_path, labels=None, threshold=0.35, model_size='tiny'):
    image = plt.imread(image_path)
    detector = obj_detector.Object_Detector_Tool(image, labels, threshold, model_size)
    objects = detector.detect()
    return objects
